records.name: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
records.summary:
This Land hosts the flashpoint of the country's 2026 prison-placement controversy: the July 2026 ruling and transfer that sent a prisoner whose legal gender had been changed under the federal Self-Determination Act to a men's prison issued from the regional court at Neubrandenburg (corroborated by multiple reports, 15-17 July 2026). The same case drove three other Länder to launch a Bundesrat initiative to tighten that Act — a framework-level event whose consequences bind prison administration, a Land competence, everywhere.

Otherwise the surviving record shows no Land-specific trans statute, placement reform, ordinance or event-security finding: a March 2026 constitutional-law survey of the 2023-26 wave of Land prison-placement reforms (placing inmates per the civil-register entry) names other Länder as reformers, not this one. Visitor exposure tracks the national framework; the placement rules bear on detained people.

records.name: Niedersachsen
records.summary:
What survives in the record for this Land is framework-level: the July 2026 prison-placement case that drove three Länder to seek a Bundesrat tightening of the federal Self-Determination Act, and a March 2026 constitutional-law survey of the quiet 2023-26 wave of Land prison-placement reforms — which does not name Niedersachsen among the reforming states.

No Lower-Saxon trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding appears in the surviving sources. In a system where criminal law and equality guarantees are federal and prison administration is a Land competence, visitor exposure here follows the national position; the placement debates concern detained people rather than visitors.
